reviewer.notes: Cross-vendor re-derivation from live probe files, not from the harvest UNIT-COMPLETE badge. Probe 1 re-ran the fixture installer: strict low ceiling refused every downgrade path at MKT-I07; misconfigured critical ceiling installed vulnerable 1.0.0 on every path; allow-vulnerable recorded the override. Probe 2 resolved a signed stale mirror that omits 1.1.0 and silently selected 1.0.0. Fresh index selected 1.1.0. The always-v2 mutant went red. Catalog asked for an Anthropic opus refuter; this box records the independent local re-derivation that actually ran.

defects.summary: A signed index has generated_at but no expiry, sequence, freshness bound, or runtime age check; a stale mirror silently omits v2 and resolves v1.
update delegates to install without a monotonic-version or minimum-version floor, so an allowed range can move an installation backward.

retry.policy: two strikes then pivot: after the second failure on the same hypothesis, enumerate at least two mechanically different attack vectors before a third attempt

residual_unknowns.claim: The real marketplace supports filesystem mirrors only; network transport replay and intermediary-cache behavior were not exercised.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: If a remote mirror transport is added, replay the same signed stale index through that adapter with a controlled response cache.

residual_unknowns.claim: The permissive advisory ceiling is a controlled misconfiguration; this run does not claim any deployed production policy has that value.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Inventory deployed trust-policy documents and compare their maximum advisory severity and override settings against the fixture values.

residual_unknowns.claim: Catalog asked for one Anthropic opus refuter; this box recorded an independent local xai re-derivation from the raw probe files.
residual_unknowns.settling_experiment: Give an Anthropic opus reviewer only the probe runner and live marketplace code, then require independently generated raw outputs.

report.title: Version downgrade attack to a known-vulnerable release
report.question_or_target: Can an attacker or a misconfiguration cause installation of an older version with a known vulnerability - through rollback, a pinned range, a mirror serving an older index, or a missing minimum-version floor?
report.answer: CONFIRMED conditionally. The strict low-severity policy refused all six downgrade routes at MKT-I07, but a critical advisory ceiling installed vulnerable v1 through every route, and the explicit allow-vulnerable override also installed it while recording the override. Independently, a signed stale mirror omitted v2 and silently resolved v1 because no freshness or expiry contract is enforced.
